patch.value: Invalidate shared history projections when writers lack SQLite

A SQLite-less append followed by a Node indexed append can certify a projection with a current stream-size receipt while omitting the middle authoritative fact. The history stream retains all three entries. Every supported runtime must participate in the invalidation protocol so a later indexed writer cannot hide earlier facts.

Reproduce two projected facts versus three authoritative facts before the fix; Preserve all three facts after a later indexed append; Exercise real Bun and Node against one isolated tracker; Keep cursor and return shapes compatible; Retain portable committed invalidation and full-source quality gates
Preserve complete shared-workspace mutation facts across SQLite and non-SQLite producers
Bun and Node can safely share the same project context without silent event omissions
The second review concurrency controls independently reproduced a missing middle event in a three-append mixed-backend sequence.
Non-SQLite writes invalidate shared projections; later indexed writes cannot certify omitted facts; repair restores all offsets without loss or duplication.
